> This can only be done through index settings providers, I believe. We have one for logsdb, may need one for tsdb just for this.

Today this is done in `IndexSortConfig`. We [hard code](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/IndexSortConfig.java#L167) the `sortSpecs` in case of logsdb and tsdb. There is no user facing api that easily shows how index sorting is setup. I think that maybe the disk usage of segments api will show hints that index sorting is active, but that is super low level.

We need to do this in a different place. We can do this using index settings providers. But maybe we can do this via index setting's default mechanism.

issue.title: Sort by pattern_text field if exists

labels.name: :StorageEngine/Mapping
labels.description: The storage related side of mappings

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
pattern_text achieves better compression if the index is sorted by the template_id of the largest pattern_text field. Sorting can be done manually with the `index.sort.*` settings, but if possible we should sort automatically. 

Specifically, we should do the following:
- if an index contains a field called `message` of type `pattern_text`:
    - if mode=logsdb and there is a host.name field: sort by host.name, message.template_id, timestamp
    - else sort by message.template_id, timestamp    

Depends on https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/129062
